Shouldn't it be Off only if all chassis are off? If we are powering off the system, it is not completely off until all the individual chassis having powered off.

Also, for both power on and power off, note that some chassis may be excluded. They might be missing, in hardware isolation, not able to communicate, etc. So the aggregation should be over the chassis that were selected for power on/power off I think? For example, if a chassis is missing, it is "Off", but that should not stop the aggregated power changing to "On" when all the present chassis finish powering on.

Yeah, good point, this commit was just On/Off, and then later in https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-state-manager/+/88977 I support the transitioning concepts and also correct what you noted here, that if any Chassis is On then the reported state will be On.


Later commits also address the presence concept (so we'll only power on/off chassis that are present). Commits not yet up yet will move to the Available concept so chassis which are unavailable for a variety of reasons will also not be included in what is logically on/off.

As noted by Matt in previous commits I probably took the "small commit" concept a bit too far here but I'd prefer to just keep things as-is for now given the end result of the patch series will address your comment here.

nit: why do we take `id` as an argument if there is only one allowed value?

Maybe there is some reason deeper into the series that i dont know about but looking ahead at 
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-state-manager/+/88929/8

it already checks `chassisId == 0` before calling `ChassisSMP` constructor.

What if we instead directly set it to `0` in the header, would it work.

Yeah, I started with the current chassis as my base and had some half hearted thoughts about some day supporting multiple SMP's within a single system but we'll wait for that to actually happen. I removed the id.
